import view

def test_basic():
    v = view.View()
    id1 = v.begin('q1')
    assert v.get_loading() == False
    # finish with same id should succeed
    rows1 = [1,2]
    assert v.finish(id1, rows1) == True
    assert v.copy_accepted_rows() == rows1
    # begin again
    id2 = v.begin('q2')
    # finish with old id should fail
    assert v.finish(id1, [3,4]) == False
    # finish with new id should succeed
    rows2 = [5,6]
    assert v.finish(id2, rows2) == True
    assert v.copy_accepted_rows() == rows2
    # begin again without finish
    id3 = v.begin('q3')
    assert v.finish(id2, [7,8]) == False
    # finish with id3 should succeed
    rows3 = [9,10]
    assert v.finish(id3, rows3) == True
    assert v.copy_accepted_rows() == rows3

def test_notes_preserved():
    v = view.View()
    v.notes[123] = 'note1'
    id1 = v.begin('q1')
    # finish without affecting notes
    v.finish(id1, [1])
    # notes still there
    assert v.notes[123] == 'note1'
    # begin again
    id2 = v.begin('q2')
    v.finish(id2, [2])
    assert v.notes[123] == 'note1'

def test_loading_and_error():
    v = view.View()
    # initially loading False
    assert v.get_loading() == False
    # begin clears loading errors
    id1 = v.begin('q1')
    # set loading True manually? spec says expose loading boolean; begin clears loading errors but keeps existing rows until valid finish.
    # We'll just check that after begin loading is False
    assert v.get_loading() == False
    # finish sets rows
    v.finish(id1, [1])
    # after finish loading should be False (spec not explicit but finish sets rows)
    # No further test needed

if __name__ == '__main__':
    test_basic()
    test_notes_preserved()
    test_loading_and_error()
    print('All tests passed')
